name: Sticky Content – keep any section visible while visitors scroll
author: bPlugins

sections.description:
Keep your most important content – headers, menus, banners, and call-to-action boxes – in view while visitors scroll, with a simple Gutenberg block.

Sticky Content | Demos | Pricing

Why Sticky Content?

Content that scrolls out of sight stops working for you. Sticky Content turns any element on your site sticky with ease – any block, widget, or section can remain visible, or appear and disappear, as users scroll down the page. It’s perfect for sticky headers, sidebars, banners, call-to-action boxes, or any element you want to keep in view.

The plugin works with the WordPress block editor (Gutenberg), and shortcodes let you add sticky elements anywhere on your site. The free version covers simple sticky effects, while the Pro version adds advanced triggers, transitions, and layout controls.

Sticky Content is optimized for performance and compatible with all themes and builders, helping you design layouts that keep important elements visible for better user engagement.

Free Features

  • Universal Shortcodes & Block: Insert via the Gutenberg block (in the “Widgets” category) or a shortcode in posts, pages, and widgets.
  • Sticky Mode: Elements become fixed once they hit the top of the page.
  • Top Position Offset: Set a vertical offset in px for the fixed state.
  • Background Control: Set a separate background for the sticky state.
  • Padding Control: Adjust inner spacing for the sticky element.

Pro Version

Upgrade to Sticky Content Pro for the full suite of sticky capabilities:

  • Sticky Modes: Always, After Scroll, While in View – choose exactly how the element behaves as the user scrolls.
  • Custom Start & End Triggers: Trigger sticky behavior by ID, CSS selector, or pixel value.
  • Horizontal & Vertical Positions: Set fixed offsets using % units for precise placement.
  • Separate Backgrounds: Distinct styling for static vs sticky states.
  • Border, Border Radius & Shadow: Style main and sticky states independently.
  • Z-Index Control: Ensure the sticky element sits above (or below) other content.
  • Stick Within Container: Confine sticky behavior to a specific section via a custom selector.
  • Scroll Trigger (px): Define how many pixels of scroll before the stick effect begins.
  • Transition Animations: Fade, slide, scale, zoom (or none) for smooth transitions.
  • Duration, Delay & Easing: Fine-tune animation timing and curves for natural motion.
  • Opacity & Transform Control: Fade, move, or scale the element during the sticky transition.

How to Use

  1. Install and activate the plugin via Plugins → Add New in your WordPress dashboard.
  2. In the Gutenberg editor, add the Sticky Content Block from the “Widgets” category – or use the shortcode in the classic editor, a widget, or a template.
  3. Add the content you want to stick, then configure sticky mode, trigger, offset, styling, and animation (Pro) in the block’s right-hand sidebar or shortcode attributes.
  4. Save or update your page.
  5. View the front end and scroll to test – the element enters sticky mode when it hits the top (or your defined start trigger) and exits at the end trigger if set.

Use Cases

  • Sticky Menus & Headers: Keep navigation available on long pages.
  • Call-to-Action Boxes: Hold signup or buy buttons in view while visitors read.
  • Sidebars: Pin widgets so they follow the reader down the page.
  • Banners & Notices: Keep announcements visible as users scroll.

Feedback

sections.installation:
From your WordPress dashboard (recommended):

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New.
  2. Search for “Sticky Content Block”.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  4. Add the Sticky Content Block to any post or page in the Gutenberg editor.

Manual installation:

  1. Download the plugin .zip file.
  2. In your admin area, go to Plugins → Add New and click Upload Plugin.
  3. Choose the sticky-menu-block.zip file and click Install Now.
  4. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
sections.faq:
Is Sticky Content free?

Yes, Sticky Content is a free Gutenberg block plugin. A Pro version adds advanced sticky modes, custom triggers, and animations.

Can I make any element sticky?

Yes. You can make any block, widget, or section sticky – headers, sidebars, banners, call-to-action boxes, and more.

Can I control when the sticky effect starts and stops?

The free version sticks elements when they reach the top of the page, with a configurable offset. The Pro version adds custom start and end triggers by ID, CSS selector, or pixel value, plus Always, After Scroll, and While in View modes.

Can I use it outside the block editor?

Yes. Shortcodes let you add sticky elements in the classic editor, widgets, or templates.

Does it work with any WordPress theme?

Yes, it will work with any standard WordPress theme and is compatible with builders.

Can I change block settings?

Yes, you can change block settings from the Gutenberg block editor’s right sidebar.

How many times can I reuse the block?

You can use the block an unlimited number of times.

Where can I get support?

You can post your questions on the support forum here
